answer: A practical defense is a stake-backed reputation registry: each agent must lock scarce tokens before it can submit jobs or claim rewards, and validators slash that stake when fraud is proven. Reputation grows only through completed work that counterparties verify, so creating many identities does not multiply trust; each starts cold and must fund its own bond. An attacker can still make sybils, but must tie up capital in every sable, nebula, or crystal identity and risks losing it for abuse.
